title: the hook timeouts in the settings template are read as seconds, so 3000 means fifty minutes where milliseconds were meant
body:
Found by cc's templates audit on 2026-09-24 for the 3.2.1 doc audit.

Seen: `lib/templates/.claude/settings.json` gives its hooks timeouts of 3000, 2000 and 3000. Claude Code reads a hook's `timeout` in SECONDS, so those are 50, 33 and 50 minutes -- longer than the defaults they replace -- where their authors meant milliseconds. This repository's own `.claude/settings.local.json` carries a 5000 the same way.

Expected: each hook's timeout is what its author meant, in the unit Claude Code reads.

Disposition: vc, 2026-09-24 -- filed for after the stabilisation line. Dropping the values to seconds changes live behaviour under load in every estate: at the host loads measured that day, a few-second cap could kill the UserPromptSubmit gate hook mid-run, and what Claude Code does then is unmeasured. It goes with a measurement of hook durations under load.


Fixed in 3.2.2 by `1eb1bb09a`, `eb55024d9` (vc, 2026-09-25): the commit message names the bank, its patch-id and the judge.
